description: Figure 3 presents three pie charts, each depicting the problem distribution categorized by difficulty level—easy, medium, and hard—and further segmented by correctness under two knowledge settings: with knowledge (w/ knowledge) and without knowledge (w/o knowledge). Each pie chart is divided into four colored slices representing the four possible combinations of correctness and knowledge availability: N+K+ (teal), N–K+ (yellow), N+K– (orange), and N–K– (red). The easy chart shows 61.5% N+K+, 34.6% N–K+, 9.8% N+K–, and 4.1% N–K–. The medium chart shows 65.4% N+K+, 30.8% N–K+, 1.5% N+K–, and 2.3% N–K–. The hard chart shows 39.6% N–K+, 30.6% N+K–, 25.1% N+K+, and 4.7% N–K–. Each slice is labeled with its corresponding percentage. The chart includes a legend to the right that maps the colors to the N+K+ through N–K– categories. The charts are arranged horizontally, with the easy, medium, and hard charts positioned from left to right, and the percentages are clearly visible within each slice. The caption indicates that while easier problems are mainly hindered by a lack of knowledge, the bottleneck for hard problems lies in geometric knowledge reasoning abilities.
